question: The Modified Kuppuswamy scale classifies socio-economic status using which combination of domains?

answers.text: Education of head of family, occupation of head of family, and monthly family income

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The Modified Kuppuswamy scale uses all three of these domains — each scored separately — to derive a composite SES class (I to V).

answers.text: Monthly per capita income, housing type, and land ownership

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These are components of the BG Prasad scale (income-based) and rural SES scales, not the Modified Kuppuswamy scale.

answers.text: Occupation, religion, and caste of the family

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Religion and caste are socio-cultural variables recorded separately during a clinico-social assessment, not components of the Kuppuswamy scoring system.

answers.text: Education of the patient, monthly family income, and number of earning members

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The Kuppuswamy scale uses the education and occupation of the head of the family (not the patient), and total monthly family income — not the count of earners.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the Modified Kuppuswamy scale. It scores three domains — education and occupation of the head of household, and total monthly family income — to classify families into SES Class I (upper) through Class V (lower).
Well done. Education + occupation of head of family + monthly family income are the three Kuppuswamy domains. Remember: income cut-offs are revised periodically to account for inflation.
